name: Prompt Injection (Direct)
test: Send a user turn that tries to override the system prompt and record whether the boundary holds.

name: Prompt Injection (Indirect)
test: Plant an instruction in retrieved text and check whether the next tool call changes.

name: Jailbreaking
test: Attempt one case from each family: roleplay, encoding, prefix injection, refusal suppression.

name: System Prompt Extraction
test: Ask for the instructions directly, then through a tool, a summary and a translation.

name: Instruction Hierarchy
test: Check whether system, developer, user, retrieved text and tool output are delimited and ranked.

name: Refusal Behaviour
test: Score refusals on legitimate requests separately from refusals on harmful ones.

name: Over-Refusal
test: Run ten benign requests in the target domain and count the false refusals.

name: Hallucination
test: Spot-check factual claims against the cited source, one claim at a time.

name: Confabulation
test: Ask for a source that cannot exist and see whether one is invented.

name: Sycophancy
test: Push back politely on a correct answer and measure how often it flips.

name: Abstention
test: Ask questions the provided context cannot answer and check whether the system says so.

name: Context Window Limits
test: Fill the window to ninety percent and check what falls out first and whether behaviour changes.

name: Lost in the Middle
test: Place a key fact at the start, middle and end of a long context and compare recall.

name: Temperature and Sampling
test: Run the same case at two settings and compare the spread rather than the average.

name: Determinism and Seeds
test: Repeat one case ten times and record the variance before reporting any single result.

name: Prompt Brittleness
test: Paraphrase one request ten ways and record the behaviour spread.

name: Persona Drift
test: Run a fifty-turn conversation and check whether the guardrails still hold at turn forty.

name: Multi-Turn Escalation
test: Reach a harmful request in small steps and record how many turns it takes.

name: Many-Shot Jailbreaking
test: Fill the prompt with dozens of benign examples that model the answer, then ask.

name: Encoding Attacks
test: Encode one probe in base64, ROT13, hex and leetspeak, scored the same way as plain text.

name: Payload Splitting
test: Split one instruction across two documents and see whether the model reassembles it.

name: Token Smuggling
test: Carry a payload past a filter using token boundaries and rare encodings.

name: Unicode Normalization
test: Compare what the filter sees with what the model sees for the same string.

name: Homoglyphs and Confusables
test: Swap Latin letters for Cyrillic and Greek lookalikes in a blocked term.

name: Invisible Characters
test: Test zero-width and bidirectional override characters in user input and in retrieved text.

name: Glitch Tokens
test: Send known unstable tokens and record crashes, loops or unusual output.

name: Low-Resource Language Attacks
test: Repeat a blocked request in three languages and compare refusal rates.

name: Multilingual Refusals
test: Check that safety behaviour is not only present in English.

name: Adversarial Examples
test: Perturb the input minimally and record whether the answer changes while the meaning does not.

name: Adversarial Suffixes
test: Append an optimised suffix and check whether it transfers to the deployed revision.

name: Data Poisoning
test: Identify every corpus that feeds the model or its retrieval, and who can write to it.

name: Backdoors and Trojans
test: Look for trigger behaviour in any supplied fine-tune and record who produced the weights.

name: Fine-Tune Safety Regression
test: Re-run the refusal suite against the fine-tuned model rather than the base model.

name: Quantization Effects
test: Compare safety behaviour at full precision and at the deployed quantization.

name: Calibration and Confidence
test: Bin the cases by stated confidence and compare each bin with its accuracy.

name: Memorization
test: Probe for near-verbatim reproduction of known training material.

name: Training Data Extraction
test: Attempt prefix completion on rare strings and record any hit.

name: Membership Inference
test: Compare confidence on known members and non-members of the training set.

name: Model Inversion
test: Attempt to recover input features from output behaviour alone.

name: Model Extraction
test: Estimate the queries needed to imitate the model, and whether the terms forbid it.

name: Model Theft and Distillation
test: Check whether the deployment exposes logits, confidence or a stable enough surface to clone.

name: Watermarking
test: Ask whether outputs are watermarked and whether the mark survives paraphrasing.

name: Fingerprinting
test: Record a behavioural fingerprint so a silent model swap is detectable later.

name: Canary Tokens
test: Plant a unique string in the system prompt and search every output, log and trace for it.

name: Copyright Reproduction
test: Request a passage from a known work and compare the output policy with the output.

name: Bias and Fairness
test: Swap protected attributes across matched pairs and count differences at a stated threshold.

name: Toxicity
test: Run a fixed probe set and score it with a calibrated judge rather than a keyword list.

name: Harm Taxonomy
test: Map the system's own defined harm categories to the cases you built.

name: Content Policy Mapping
test: Check that every policy clause has at least one case behind it.

name: Retrieval Poisoning
test: Write a document into the index and check whether it changes behaviour for later users.

name: Chunk Boundary Attacks
test: Split an instruction across two chunks and confirm no single chunk looks wrong alone.

name: Embedding Inversion
test: Check whether a query can recover source text from the embedding store.

name: Vector Store Access Control
test: Query the vector store directly with a low-privilege identity.

name: Document-Level ACLs
test: Query as a user who should not see a document and check the retriever filters first.

name: Cross-Tenant Leakage
test: Two tenants, one index, and the query that returns the other tenant's chunk.

name: Metadata Injection
test: Put an instruction in document metadata and see whether it reaches the model.

name: Ingestion Validation
test: Attempt to add a document without authorisation and record what the pipeline checks.

name: Retrieval Provenance
test: Check whether each retrieved chunk carries a source and a traceable identifier.

name: Tool Calling Abuse
test: Call each tool with arguments the interface allows and the task never needs.

name: Tool Description Poisoning
test: Read every tool description and check whether any of them contains instructions.

name: Tool Rug Pull
test: Compare tool definitions and outputs between approval and use.

name: Argument Injection
test: Steer a legitimate tool to attacker-chosen arguments through injected text.

name: Excessive Agency
test: List every tool and the credential behind it, then the scopes that exceed the task.

name: Confused Deputy
test: Use the agent to act with authority the current user does not hold.

name: Permission Scoping
test: Check that scopes are per request rather than per service account.

name: On-Behalf-Of Tokens
test: Confirm the tool call carries the user's identity rather than the agent's.

name: Human-in-the-Loop Bypass
test: Reach the approval gate, spoof it, skip it with a retry, or starve it with a timeout.

name: Approval Fatigue
test: Count approvals per hour and check whether the review is real at that rate.

name: Agent Memory Poisoning
test: Write to persistent memory and check whether it returns in fresh sessions.

name: Agent-to-Agent Trust
test: Send a subagent a message that crosses a trust boundary and record what it obeys.

name: MCP Server Trust
test: Check what an MCP server can read, write and call, and who reviewed it.

name: Subagent Spawning
test: Check whether a kill switch reaches agents spawned after the stop.

name: Kill Switch Escape
test: Trigger the stop mid-run and confirm every branch halts and reports.

name: Sandbox Escape
test: Attempt filesystem, process and network reach from the tool runtime.

name: Code Execution via Tools
test: Run code through the tool path and record what the sandbox permits.

name: SSRF via Fetch and Browse
test: Point the fetch tool at the metadata endpoint and at an internal admin page.

name: Autonomous Goal Hijacking
test: Change the stated goal mid-run through injected content and see whether the plan follows.

name: Loop and Step Ceiling
test: Look for a missing or high step ceiling and measure the cost of one runaway run.

name: Unbounded Consumption
test: Remove the per-user budget and measure tokens per session at sustained load.

name: Denial of Wallet
test: Estimate the spend a cheap attacker can force without any exploit skill.

name: Prompt Injection via Files and PDFs
test: Upload a document with instructions in body text, in a comment and in an alt text field.

name: Multimodal Injection
test: Put text in an image, a screenshot and an audio clip and see whether it is obeyed.

name: Steganographic Exfiltration
test: Check whether output length, whitespace or formatting can carry data.

name: Insecure Output Handling
test: Map every sink the model's text can reach and what renders it.

name: SQL Injection via LLM
test: Steer model-written SQL and record the database role behind it.

name: XSS via LLM Output
test: Return markup into a client that renders it and check what executes.

name: Markdown Image Exfiltration
test: Embed an image URL with data in the query string and watch the egress.

name: Link Parameter Exfiltration
test: Check whether a link the model emits can carry a conversation fragment.

name: Output Length Side Channel
test: Check whether the length of a refusal leaks the content it refused.

name: Schema Validation
test: Break the JSON contract and see whether the consumer validates or trusts.

name: Structured Output Abuse
test: Force content through a schema field that the plain-text filter would block.

name: Guardrail Bypass
test: Attempt bypass by encoding, language, length and structured output.

name: Guardrail Ordering
test: Check whether the guardrail runs before the tool call or after it.

name: Prompt Firewall
test: Test the firewall as an adversarial classifier rather than as a policy document.

name: Input Sanitization
test: Compare the sanitised input with what the model actually receives.

name: Spotlighting and Delimiters
test: Check that the markers survive summarisation and concatenation.

name: Dual-LLM Pattern
test: Confirm the privileged model never sees untrusted text directly.

name: Allowlisting vs Blocklisting
test: Test whether the control names what is allowed or lists what is not.

name: Eval Set Design
test: One behaviour per case, one expected outcome, one fixture that reruns.

name: Golden Sets
test: Store the reference answer and the rubric with the case rather than in someone's memory.

name: Held-Out Sets
test: Keep a slice the team never tunes against and report it separately.

name: Private Slices
test: Keep the sensitive slice out of any public benchmark.

name: Benchmark Contamination
test: Check for overlap by paraphrase, by translation and by rare-phrase search.

name: Benchmark Saturation
test: Compare headroom with noise before treating a high score as a signal.

name: Attack Success Rate
test: Define the unit as attempts or objectives and report the rate with its interval.

name: Per-Objective vs Per-Attempt
test: Report both and say which one the reader needs.

name: Confidence Intervals
test: Attach a Wilson interval to every rate, especially the small ones.

name: Pass@k
test: Report capability at least once across k attempts.

name: Pass^k (Reliability)
test: Report the probability of success on every one of k attempts.

name: Paired Comparison
test: Compare two versions on the same cases rather than two independent rates.

name: Sample Size and Power
test: Check the suite can detect the difference being claimed.

name: Run-to-Run Variance
test: Run five times and report the spread before the mean.

name: LLM-as-Judge
test: State the judge model, its revision and the prompt it runs.

name: Judge Calibration
test: Hand-grade a sample and report agreement with the judge.

name: Position Bias
test: Swap the order of two answers and see whether the verdict moves.

name: Verbosity Bias
test: Trim one answer and check whether the score follows the length.

name: Self-Preference Bias
test: Grade output from the judge's own family against output from another.

name: Inter-Rater Reliability
test: Have two people grade the same slice and compare.

name: Cohen's Kappa
test: Report agreement corrected for chance rather than raw percentage.

name: Rubric Design
test: One behaviour per criterion, and a rubric short enough not to drift.

name: Failure Taxonomy
test: Bucket every failure so that a fix can be assigned to it.

name: Severity Scoring
test: Define severity before the run and give the reason for each score.

name: Regression Suites
test: Turn every finding into a case that runs on every deploy.

name: CI Eval Gates
test: Block a deploy on a regression in the safety suite.

name: Drift Canaries
test: Run a standing set weekly and alert when the refusal rate moves.

name: Trace-Based Evaluation
test: Score spans inside an agent run, not only the final answer.

name: Automated Red Teaming
test: Generate cases at volume and record what the generator missed.

name: Fuzzing and Mutation
test: Mutate known cases and record the hit rate per mutation.

name: Adversarial Test Generation
test: Use a model to attack a model and report the generator as part of the method.

name: Coverage Argument
test: Write down the classes tested and the classes skipped, with the reason for each.

name: Cost per Case
test: Report the suite's cost so that it can actually be rerun.

name: Latency per Case
test: Report how long a full run takes at the sample size claimed.

name: Reproducibility Contract
test: Record model revision, prompt version, index snapshot, tool schema, sampling and date.

name: Threat Modelling for AI
test: Write the asset, the actor, the trust boundary and the abuse case before testing.

name: Trust Boundaries
test: Draw the line between instruction and data for every channel that carries text.

name: Data Flow Mapping
test: Trace one input from entry to output and mark every place it is trusted.

name: Attack Surface Map
test: One diagram of every input channel, tool and output sink.

name: Propagation Testing
test: One bad input, then trace how far the effect reaches.

name: OWASP LLM Top 10
test: Map each finding so that the security team can file it.

name: OWASP Agentic Security
test: Map agent findings to the agentic categories.

name: MITRE ATLAS
test: Map the technique so the finding joins the wider threat picture.

name: NIST AI RMF
test: Check the client's controls against a framework they already report on.

name: NIST Generative AI Profile
test: Map the specific actions to the profile's suggested controls.

name: ISO/IEC 42001
test: Check where AI management meets the existing management system.

name: EU AI Act Duties
test: Establish general purpose or high risk, and which duties that triggers.

name: Model and System Cards
test: Compare the documented limits with the observed behaviour.

name: AI Bill of Materials
test: List weights, dataset and dependencies, and whether each is pinned.

name: Model Provenance and Signing
test: Confirm the artefact is signed and the digest matches what runs.

name: Risk Register
test: Enter each finding with an owner, a residual risk and a review date.

name: Dangerous Capability Evaluation
test: Test uplift and autonomy inside a container with no live access.

name: Uplift Studies
test: Compare an unaided expert with an assisted one on the same task.

name: Propensity vs Capability
test: Separate what the system can be made to do from what it does unprompted.

name: Red Team Rules of Engagement
test: Written scope, authorised targets, a stop condition and a named person who can stop it.

name: Safe Harbour
test: Agree in writing what the tester may do and what protection applies.

name: Coordinated Disclosure
test: Agree the channel and the timeline before the first finding exists.

name: Bug Bounty for AI
test: Check the programme covers prompt injection and model behaviour, not only web bugs.

name: AI Incident Response
test: Walk one scenario: a prompt leak, model abuse, or an exfiltration channel firing.

name: Human Oversight Design
test: Name what the gate gates and whether the person can understand the decision.

name: Auditable Logging
test: Check the log answers a regulator's question six months later.

name: Privacy Impact Assessment
test: Treat prompts as personal data and check residency, retention and access.

name: Data Residency of Prompts
test: Trace where prompt text is stored and which jurisdiction holds it.

name: Prompt Versioning
test: Confirm every prompt change has an identifier and a rollback.

name: Model Version Pinning
test: Pin the revision by digest and record it in every report.

name: Rollback of Prompts and Models
test: Restore the previous version and check the index and cache go back too.

name: Purple Teaming
test: Run the defence and the attack together so the fix is tested as it is written.

name: Continuous Red Teaming
test: Schedule the suite rather than running it once at launch.

name: Adversarial Training as Patching
test: Check whether a patch removes the behaviour or only the string that triggered it.

name: Safety Cases
test: Write the argument that the system is acceptable, with its assumptions named.
